newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH MINISTRY PLANS BUDVAR STAKE SALE TO MANAGERS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH MINISTRY PLANS BUDVAR STAKE SALE TO MANAGERS.

text.p: The Czech Agriculture Ministry expects to submit a plan to the cabinet in February to partially privatise the brewery Budejovicky Budvar n.p.> through a management buyout, a senior ministry official said on Tuesday.

The chief of the ministry's privatisation department, Jiri Stehlik, told Reuters that the plan would be to sell a 10 percent stake to the brewer's management with an option for them to buy eventually another 41 percent.
"This is the proposal of the resort, but the government decides on it, so it can change," Stehlik said.
He said that the plan did not include a foreign partner to take part in the first stage of the privatisation process, but added that it did not exclude that later entry of a foreign investor.
Stehlik declined to give further details of the plan's structure.
Budvar, 100 percent state owned, is the maker of the Czech version of "Budweiser", its flagship label.
The governemnt had delayed privatisation of the company while trying to set a trademark dispute with Anheuser-Busch Cos. , makers of the U.S. version of Budweiser,
But talks with Busch, which was seeking a minority stake in Budvar, were broken off last year.

The negotiations over the use of the "Budweiser" and "Bud" trademarks were aimed at resolving a long-standing disagreement which prohibits the rivals from selling their labels in the other's key markets.
Anheuser-Busch sells its beer under the Budweiser name in 11 European countries and under the "Bud" name in nine other European countries.
Budvar is one of the five largest Czech breweries, and Budweiser is one of the country's best-known exports.
The Czech government considers Budvar as a part of the "family silver".
